segmentation.text: It is unlawful for the driver of any vehicle:
To fail to obey an official traffic-control device or the directions of a police officer

elements.justification: "vehicle" is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle, "every device in, upon or by which any person or property is or may be transported or drawn upon a highway"; "driver" (DEF-NRS-484A-080) is a role read through the vehicle's controlled motion.

"Official traffic-control device" (DEF-NRS-484A-145) is "every sign, signal, marking and device ... placed or erected by a public authority or railroad for the purpose of regulating, warning or guiding traffic"; at a railroad crossing its members that direct the subject's entry are dev.railway_signal_or_gate ("the devices at a level crossing; lights in {flashing, dark}; gate in {up, lowering, down, raising, none}": obeyed by not entering while the lights flash or the gate is not up), dev.traffic_signal (circular_red: not entering), dev.stop_sign ("regulatory sign requiring a full halt": a halt, drv.motion.complete_halt, on the approach short of the crossing, within p.railroad_crossing_approach_reach by st.region_geometry) and dev.yield_sign ("requiring yielding without a mandatory halt": not entering while a rail vehicle, ru.rail_vehicle, closes within the conflict horizon — prim.closest_approach_within and prim.closest_approach_distance, which are "not a stand-in for contact" and are read only as the conflict bound). "Police officer" (DEF-NRS-484A-180, "every officer authorized to direct or regulate traffic") is dev.human_direction of role police_officer; its indication stop is obeyed by not entering. Each device must govern (dev.governs, "the travel regions whose traffic the device controls") a travel region (st.travel_region) the subject occupies (rel.occupies) at its entry; dev.governs is not a position, and the place of the halt is read from the distance to the crossing.

The device or direction is obeyed at a railroad crossing: the event judged is the subject's entry into a st.railway_crossing, "level crossing of a railway with the roadway, and its nearest rail", the observation at which its footprint comes to overlap it (rel.occupies) having not overlapped it at the previous one. "Railroad" (DEF-NRS-484A-200) excludes streetcars, which form no level crossing of a railway with the roadway.

applicability: The subject is a vehicle and enters a railroad crossing c at this observation: rises(rel.occupies(subject, c)) for some st.railway_crossing c.
obligation: At the entry observation, for every device d that governs (dev.governs) a travel region r the subject occupies at that observation: (i) d a dev.railway_signal_or_gate: its lights are not flashing and its gate is not lowering, down or raising; (ii) d a dev.traffic_signal: it does not display circular_red; (iii) d a dev.human_direction of role police_officer: its indication is not stop; (iv) d a dev.yield_sign: no rail vehicle q (ru.rail_vehicle) has prim.closest_approach_within(subject, q) over p.conflict_horizon with prim.closest_approach_distance at most p.conflict_centre_clearance; (v) d a dev.stop_sign: the subject halted before this entry. For (v) the search runs back from the entry: a halt counts at an observation where drv.motion.complete_halt(subject) holds with speed_tol p.halt_speed_tolerance, the subject's footprint does not overlap c, and its body is within p.railroad_crossing_approach_reach of c (st.region_geometry). The search ends at the last observation before the entry at which the subject's body was farther from c than p.railroad_crossing_approach_reach (the approach start: only an observed exit from that zone begins a new approach), or at the previous entry of the subject into c. Finding the halt meets the duty; reaching either end without it violates it; where the recording begins with the subject already within the reach of c and no halt is observed since, or the distance to c is unobserved at an observation the search reads and no halt is found, the duty is unknown. Where no device governs a region the subject occupies at the entry, the duty is complied with.

narrowings.why: "the driver" is read through the vehicle's controlled motion; whoever or whatever controls it.
That a device is official, placed by a public authority or railroad, is read from its presence.

Obedience is read at the subject's entry into the crossing, through the devices and directions that govern that entry (railway lights and gate, a red signal, a stop or yield sign, a police officer's stop); instructions that do not bear on entering the crossing, and a direction to proceed, are not read.

scenarios.name: forbid
scenarios.narrative: Railway signal lights flashing, gate down, governing the subject's approach lane; the subject car drives around the gate and its footprint comes to overlap the railway crossing.

scenarios.name: permit
scenarios.narrative: Railway signal lights dark, gate up, governing the subject's lane; the subject car enters the crossing.

scenarios.name: idle
scenarios.narrative: The subject car drives along a street with no railway crossing; it never overlaps one.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: The subject car enters a crossing; a railway signal with lights flashing stands at the crossing but the source does not observe which regions it governs.

scenarios.name: branch_1
scenarios.narrative: A stop sign governs the subject's lane at the crossing; the subject car approaches from 60 m, halts 6 m from the crossing (kin.speed 0), then enters.

scenarios.name: branch_2
scenarios.narrative: A stop sign governs the subject's lane; the subject approaches from 60 m and enters the crossing at 8 m/s without halting.

scenarios.name: branch_3
scenarios.narrative: A police officer (dev.human_direction role police_officer, indication stop) governs the subject's lane; the subject enters the crossing.

scenarios.name: branch_4
scenarios.narrative: The subject enters an unsignalled crossing with no device governing its lane; no other road user in the scene.

scenarios.name: history_boundary
scenarios.narrative: A stop sign governs the subject's lane; the recording begins with the subject 10 m from the crossing moving at 3 m/s, no halt is observed, and it enters the crossing.
scenarios.boundary: the subject's approach to the crossing from beyond p.railroad_crossing_approach_reach, which lies before the recording's first observation

param_proposals.name: p.railroad_crossing_approach_reach
param_proposals.convention: the ground distance from a vehicle's body to a railroad grade crossing within which the vehicle is at the crossing, on the stretch where a halt for the crossing is made: the 50-ft outer bound of the zone in which grade-crossing practice places the halt before the nearest rail
param_proposals.source: MUTCD Part 8 highway-rail grade crossing stop-line placement and the Uniform Vehicle Code grade-crossing stop zone

param_proposals.name: p.halt_speed_tolerance
param_proposals.convention: the speed at or below which a sampled speed counts as no movement: the source's speed resolution
param_proposals.source: speed resolution of vehicle tracking sources

param_proposals.name: p.conflict_horizon
param_proposals.convention: time-to-collision threshold of the traffic-conflict technique: a closest approach later than this is not a present danger of a crash

param_proposals.name: p.conflict_centre_clearance
param_proposals.convention: centre-to-centre distance at the closest approach below which the bodies of a passenger car and another road user are taken to collide or nearly collide: about a car's half-length plus half a body width
